meanings.note: About any elderly woman.

examples.text: Она с бабушкой живёт. Бабушка болеет всё время.
examples.trans: She lives with her grandmother. Grandma is ill all the time.

examples.text: Ну ладно, давай беги. Бабушке привет!
examples.trans: Okay, off you go. Say hi to Grandma!
What a progressive granny you are!

meanings.note: Больной ребёнок = a sick child.
colloquial insult: ты больной? = are you crazy?

examples.text: Вы взяточник! Вы лезете вперёд больного ребёнка.
examples.trans: You're a bribe-taker! You're pushing in ahead of a sick child.

meanings.note: with a past-tense verb: я бы подумал = I would think
wishes: купили бы = we could have bought

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief.
+ dative of person + accusative of thing
+ infinitive: не даёт мне готовить
imperative давай/давайте + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

related.gloss: to hand in; to take (an exam)

meanings.note: 'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: Colloquial.

examples.text: У меня дед три года партизанил!
examples.trans: My grandfather was a partisan for three years!
My grandfather lives in the country.

examples.text: Я никого пытать не буду, ясно? У меня дед три года партизанил!
examples.trans: I'm not going to torture anyone, got it? My grandfather was a partisan for three years!

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: A fact or a person.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Parenthetical. Core Russian adv meaning 'so, then, that means' in everyday speech.
verb: Что это значит? = What does it mean?

examples.text: Катя, мне надо тебе кое-что сказать.
examples.trans: Katya, I need to tell you something.
I want to show you something.

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Уже месяц = for a month now.

examples.trans: I've been living here for a month.
The election is in a month.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.
You both leave here right now.
Get over here right now, quickly, both of you!

examples.text: Вы сейчас отсюда оба уходите. И больше сюда не возвращаетесь. Ясно?
examples.trans: You both leave here right now. And you never come back here again. Clear?

meanings.en: to cheat, to deceive, to trick
meanings.note: Меня обманули = I've been cheated.

examples.trans: If you cheat us, there'll be trouble.
Listen, if you cheat us, there'll be trouble. Got it?

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.note: ничего не осталось = there's nothing left

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.en: match (in a relationship: я не пара вам = I'm no match for you)

examples.text: Я понимаю, я не пара вам.
examples.trans: I understand I'm no match for you.
They are a very handsome couple.

examples.text: Я понимаю, я не пара вам. Вы красавец, а я старая.
examples.trans: I understand I'm no match for you. You're a handsome man, and I'm old.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Поговорить с + instrumental. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить').

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Всё понятно = all clear.
As a reply.

examples.trans: I'm going to be mayor, understood?

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Серьёзно? = really?.
once; что скажешь? = what do you say?
Polite request. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать').

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
To someone you call ты. Core Russian det meaning 'your (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: As opposed to before.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

хотя.gloss: even if, at least (with бы); although

meanings.note: нужно хотя бы поговорить = we need at least to talk

examples.text: Нужно хотя бы поговорить с ними.
examples.trans: We need at least to talk with them.

examples.text: Вы плохо поступили, но хотя бы совесть есть.
examples.trans: You acted badly, but at least you have a conscience.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!
